archetype

AR-kih-type -- three syllables, stress on the first syllable, AR; the 'ch' sounds like a K. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Archetype is the original model or most typical example that others are patterned on.

The lone gunslinger who rides in to save a helpless town is the archetype of the Western hero.

Worked Example

For a class project, Priya lines up Cinderella, Snow White, and three brand-new animated movies. In every single one she finds the same figure: a vain older woman who secretly torments the young heroine. Five different films, five different faces -- one unmistakable pattern underneath.

Priya has found an archetype: the wicked-stepmother figure is an original character pattern that storytellers have reused for centuries. An archetype is the master template -- later characters are built from it and measured against it, the way every movie detective still stands in Sherlock Holmes's shadow.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

template: A template is a preset pattern reused again and again, stamping out much the same result each time. An archetype leaves far more room: later examples can grow very different and still descend from it, the way every fictional detective descends from Sherlock Holmes.

blueprint: A blueprint is the detailed plan a thing is built from, drawn up before the thing exists. An archetype stands farther back: not a drafted plan for one product, but the founding example that a whole family of later works grows out of.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

copy: a reproduction of an original

imitation: something made to resemble another thing

Where it sits · how completely it shapes what follows — model → archetype → mold

model vs. archetype: Model says only that something is worth following -- a role model, a model answer -- while an archetype is the founding pattern its whole category grows from.

mold vs. archetype: Mold is the strongest image of the three: things from the same mold come out practically identical, and calling a character 'cast from the old mold' says the archetype shaped every inch of it.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — arche-

prefix — arche-: first, original (Greek arkhe 'beginning')

root — type

root — type: stamp, model, impression (Greek typos)

Put it together

Put it together: Archetype is Greek for 'the first stamp' -- arkhe ('first, original') plus typos ('stamp, model'). Picture the very first stamp ever carved: every print made afterward carries its shape. That is what an archetype is -- the original impression from which all the later copies take their form.

Use the root in a new word: archaeology

Use the root in a new word: archaeology: Through archaeology, the team pieced together how the city's first settlers lived.

Root Check

Word Choice

Keep archetype apart from its unit-mate epitome. The archetype is the original pattern that later examples are modeled on and judged against -- Sherlock Holmes is the archetype of the detective, and every later sleuth descends from him. The epitome is the finest embodiment of a quality -- your neighbor can be the epitome of patience without anyone copying her. If later examples copy it, it's an archetype; if it simply shows a quality at its very best, it's an epitome.
